A Most Valuable Poster (MVP) is a player who has answered players' questions consistently and accurately in the past such that Blizzard Entertainment gives a note of credibility to what they post. They continue to promote constructive posting wherever they can. They contribute to the community and encourage polite discussion throughout the forums. When you see an MVP post, listen to what they have to say — they were chosen for their knowledge of the game, also. The MVP program is not to say that no one else is helpful, nor that MVPs are 100% helpful. But for the sake of the new player asking a question, the MVP title means "This poster is likely telling you the truth with the intent of

A game account management feature that allows you to move some characters from one Realm to another. Only some realms are eligible for movement. Eligible realms are announced periodically by Blizzard. All transfers are between similar servers: PvP to PvP, RP to RP, Normal (PvE) to Normal, and presumably RP-PvP to RP-PvP. See also: * [http://www.worldofwarcraft.com/info/faq/charactermove.html Official Character Transfer F.A.Q.]. * [http://www.worldofwarcraft.com/info/faq/charactermove-list.html Official List of Eligible Realms and Move Character option].

Move To is a pet command that sends the pet to a location and commands it to stay there. The location is selected via a targeting reticule. The two pet movement commands Follow and Move To are mutually exclusive, and one is always active on a pet at any given time. Outside of combat, a pet commanded to Move To a location will stay at that location, regardless of its master's movements. However, pets set to Move To will still follow normal behaviour rules set by their stance (Assist, Defensive or Passive) and respond to the Attack command; attacks by the player (for Assist), upon the player (for Assist or Defensive), or the command to Attack will all cause the pet to attack the appropriate ta

Little did he know that his son would be kidnapped and forced to work for the Bloodsail Buccaneers. When word reached the Defias Brotherhood that their son was plundering ships, they kidnapped him and his wife. They would eventually be freed and returned to the farm along with their son.

Mr. Pinchy's Blessing is a buff randomly gained when using the Mr. Pinchy item. This counts as a flask item, meaning it persists through death, and also counts as a Guardian and Battle Elixir. Previous to 2.1.0, this buff gave 1200 HP, the same as a Flask of the Titans. The buff is now 500 HP, 100 HP more than the current Titans flask, but does not have the 10 Defense Rating bonus the Flask of Fortification offers.

shamans in Arathi Basin-battleground.]] Multiboxing is a term used to denote one user playing multiple accounts simultaneously. This could be done using one or more machines. Some players ran multiple accounts to seek a greater challenge than playing only a single character. Others sought to recreate the feel of older single-player RPGs where a well designed team was used to adventure together. There were also some who didn't want to rely on others to play the game when additional characters were required. Mulgore is a level 1—10 zone for Horde players. Players travel through the zone, battling the quilboar and completing the Rites of the Earthmother to become true tauren braves. Unlike many other non-instanced starting areas (which, for the most part, can be done by any race), more than half of Mulgore storyline is only doable by tauren characters.

Mudmug's Place is the home of Mudmug found in east-central Valley of the Four Winds. The small farm turned home brewery is found along the road between the Thunderfoot Fields off to the east and Halfhill to the west. Just to the north of his home is the Sunsoaked Meadow, where the virmen are coming from. Mudmug uses muddy water with bugs that ferment the ale he makes, however, he has begun having issues with the local Twitchheel virmen.

Mudmug, whose real name unknown, is a somewhat crazy pandaren brewmaster who lives at Mudmug's Place in the Valley of the Four Winds. He got his nickname for the way he brews his beer — using muddy water, rather than fermentation from yeast. After the player helps him to obtain muddy water for his brews and to deal with virmen infestation, he joins Chen Stormstout and Li Li on their journey to Halfhill and eventually to the Stormstout Brewery, eventually helping them get rid of the virmen, hozen and alementals that have been wreaking havoc at the brewery.
